# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection — 10.2.28.88 (DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR)

## Evidence Reviewed
- `2026-02-28-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (15,512 frames). No IDS/Suricata alert exports were present in the evidence directory; attribution below is based entirely on traffic behavior.

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.2.28.88 | dominant local talker in `conv,ip`; source of all C2 traffic |
| MAC | 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad | ARP: `arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.2.28.88` bound to this MAC |
| Hostname | DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR | NBNS name registration from 10.2.28.88; also seen in DHCP option 12 hostname |
| Domain | easyas123.tech (AD domain, DC at 10.2.28.2 / EASYAS123-DC.easyas123.tech) | DNS SRV/LDAP queries for `_ldap._tcp...easyas123.tech`, NBNS `EASYAS123<1d>` from 10.2.28.2 |
| Logged-in user | brolf | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS traffic between 10.2.28.88 and 10.2.28.2 |

## Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** (commercial NetSupport Manager remote-control software abused as a RAT). **Attribution: behavioral**, based on:
- HTTP `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` on every beacon (264 POSTs observed).
- The C2 protocol payload matches NetSupport's known check-in grammar exactly: decoded POST bodies begin `CMD=POLL\nINFO=1\nACK=1\n`, and server responses/subsequent client POSTs use `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<hex-encoded blob>` — this is the documented NetSupport Client32 (`client32.exe`) beacon/keepalive and encrypted-data-channel format.
- Traffic uses port 443 but is plaintext HTTP (no TLS ClientHello on that port/stream), consistent with NetSupport RAT's common configuration of using 443 for cover without actually wrapping in TLS.
- No third-party IDS signature was available to confirm the family name; this call is made from the UA string and protocol grammar alone, so it is not signature-confirmed.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint:**
- `45.131.214.85:443` (TCP, plaintext HTTP, not TLS) — sustained beaconing from 10.2.28.88:51912 over the length of the capture (~15,637s duration, 550 frames), evidenced by `conv,ip` output and 264 POST requests captured via `http.request && ip.dst==45.131.214.85`.

**Malicious domain:**
- `vadusa.xyz` — queried twice by 10.2.28.88 (frames 1559, 1747) and resolved by the internal DNS server (10.2.28.2) to `45.131.214.85` in frame 2566 (`dns.a==45.131.214.85`). TCP session to that IP begins at frame 2569, immediately after resolution.

**Malicious URL:**
- `http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm` — the fixed C2 checkpoint URI for all 264 POST requests (`http.request.method==POST && ip.dst==45.131.214.85`).

**Malware protocol markers (grounded in traffic, useful as detection content):**
- HTTP User-Agent string `NetSupport Manager/1.3` on all requests to the C2.
- POST body plaintext prefix `CMD=POLL\nINFO=1\nACK=1\n` (decoded from `http.file_data` in frame 2638) and `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=...` (frames 2639+) for the encrypted command/data channel.

**File names / hashes:** None. No executable, script, or archive transfer to or from 10.2.28.88 was observed in this capture (`--export-objects http` yielded only benign Microsoft/Adobe update artifacts — see below). The initial infection/delivery vector is **not captured** in this pcap; the capture begins after the RAT is already resident and beaconing.

## Benign Context (not IOCs)
- Windows/Microsoft telemetry and update infrastructure: `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `edge.microsoft.com`, `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`, `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `api.msn.com`, `assets.msn.com`, `oneclient.sfx.ms`, `ocsp.digicert.com`.
- Adobe update check: `acroipm2.adobe.com/assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt`.
- Internal AD/domain traffic: LDAP/Kerberos/SMB2/DCE-RPC/NBNS between 10.2.28.88 and the domain controller 10.2.28.2 (EASYAS123-DC.easyas123.tech).
- NVIDIA GFE (`services.gfe.nvidia.com`), Google update service (`update.googleapis.com`), Google Fonts/network-time (`deff.nelreports.net`).

## Incident Summary
The Windows workstation **DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR** (10.2.28.88, MAC 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad), logged in as domain user **brolf** on the **easyas123.tech** AD domain, is infected with **NetSupport RAT**. The malware resolved the attacker-registered domain **vadusa.xyz** to **45.131.214.85** and established a persistent, long-duration HTTP beacon (not TLS, despite using port 443) to **`http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm`**, sending 264 `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` check-ins identified by the `NetSupport Manager/1.3` User-Agent and NetSupport's characteristic command grammar. The capture does not include the initial delivery/infection vector; only post-compromise C2 beaconing is present.
